newsitem.title: CHINA: Cheung Kong's Jardine buy not hostile -China paper.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong's Jardine buy not hostile -China paper.

text.p: Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd seems to be interested in the Jardine group's Hong Kong properties and not in a takeover of the group, Beijing- controlled newspaper Wen Wei Po said on Wednesday.

News on Tuesday that Cheung Kong and its Hutchison Whampoa Ltd unit together held a 3.03 percent stake in Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd and a 3.06 percent stake in Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd sparked speculation that a takeover bid could be on the way.
"The possibility of a hostile takeover bid is non-existent," Wen Wei Po said in its editorial.

It pointed to the Jardine group's anti-takeover mechanism which was put in place after an unsuccessful raid on Hongkong Land in 1987. The newspaper said Cheung Kong and Hutchison would not aim for something which was unachievable.
It said Cheung Kong probably had its eye on Hongkong Land's office portfolio in Central, Hong Kong's business district.
Hongkong Land is the largest landlord in Central.

"It is a good idea to redevelop Hongkong Land's old office towers in Central since the Central station of the airport railway will start operation in April, 1998 and such a plan would have good prospects," it said.
The Mass Transit Railway Corp is building a new railway from Central to Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok airport.
Wen Wei Po said Cheung Kong had been able to pick up Hongkong Land shares at a big discount to net asset value.
Hongkong Land shares have lagged the stocks of Hong Kong property developers since they listed in London and Singapore.
"Shares of Hongkong Land will continue to trade below the Hong Kong market level and lack vitality if they are not relisted in Hong Kong," Wen Wei Po said.
Jardine Matheson withdrew the secondary listing of the company from the Hong Kong Stock Exchange at the end of 1994 and Hongkong Land delisted at thd end of March 1995.
Both companies moved their domicile to Bermuda from Hong Kong after a Sino-British treaty was signed in 1984 which set out the terms of Hong Kong's return to China on July 1, 1997.

Wen Wei Po said Jardine had misjudged post-handover Hong Kong. The "one country two systems" formula allowing Hong Kong to keep its capitalist lifestyle for 50 years after the transfer of sovereignty had inspired confidence in the territory.
It said Jardine now understood this and getting back to Hong Kong was a hot subject for the group.
It said evidence of Jardine's renewed confidence in the territory has been displayed with the group's re-emergence at Hong Kong's government land auction.

"Jardine has said it welcomed friendly investments of Hong Kong Chinese companies and this is a prelude to reshaping the company into a new image as well as a preparation for a relisting in Hong Kong," it said. -- Hong Kng News Room (852) 2843 6369
